ArmourLight and medium armour. Heavier armour only through training, like any class. Infusers are trained in all armour and shields (see Kit).
BtH+1 per 6 levels (+2 at 12th, +4 at 24th)
KitAt character creation choose a Kit — Infuser, Construct Engineer, Gadgeteer, or Alchemist. All Kits share the same baseline chassis below; the Kit determines exactly what your Ingenuity Points build.
IdentityAn inventor who brings the workshop into every fight: a Spark Caster in hand and a discipline of gadgets, infusions, constructs or brews.

Level by Level at a Glance

What you gain and when. Full details are under Class Abilities.

LvlYou gain

Class Abilities

1st Level

Tinker's Craft (Intelligence)

  • Effect: The shared skill of building, repairing, identifying, and jury-rigging mechanisms and minor magic items. You are Trained in it at 1st level and a Master at 5th. Roll it as a Skill (Book II). An hour's work reveals one property of an item, as Identify.

Ingenuity Points

  • Effect: A daily pool equal to Intelligence modifier + Artificer level (minimum 1) that fuels your Kit's abilities. Recovers fully on a long rest.
  • Kit Feature (1st): gain the 1st-tier ability from your chosen Kit

First Creation

  • Effect: You begin play with one item already made, chosen freely from your Kit's Known list in The Artificer's Workshop, with no Ingenuity Point cost and no crafting time spent.
  • An Infuser starts with one item already infused (the infusion lasts as normal and can be renewed the usual way once it ends); a Gadgeteer starts with one gadget already built and ready to use; an Alchemist starts with one formula already brewed and in their pack.
  • A Construct Engineer instead starts with one Modular Chassis mount already installed on their companion at no cost, on top of the companion itself.

Spark Caster

  • Effect: You carry a hand-built repeater, powered by an arcanite shard, that only you can work.
  • As an attack, fire it at one creature within 60ft: it makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC, taking force damage on a failure or half on a success, as a Warlock's Eldritch Blast.
  • The damage is 1d6 (1d8 at 5th, 2d6 at 9th, 2d8 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th, 3d8 at 24th) plus your Intelligence modifier.
  • It counts as a magic weapon and fires once a round even if you gain Extra Attack.

2nd Level

Quick Hands

  • Effect: Using an infused item, gadget or formula can be part of your action: use one and also make one weapon attack, fire your Spark Caster or cast one cantrip you have from elsewhere with the same action. A damaging formula or gadget can't be used with the Spark Caster in the same action.

3rd Level

  • Kit Feature (3rd): gain the 3rd-tier ability from your chosen Kit

4th Level

Salvage

  • Effect: Once per day, spend 10 minutes tinkering to regain Ingenuity Points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).

5th Level

  • Kit Feature (5th): gain the 5th-tier ability from your chosen Kit

6th Level

Overclock

  • Effect: Spend 2 extra Ingenuity Points on a damaging Kit effect to roll its dice twice and keep the higher result, for one roll of that effect.

7th Level

  • Kit Feature (7th): gain the 7th-tier ability from your chosen Kit

10th Level

  • Lasting Work: gain the permanent-item-creation ability from your chosen Kit: every Kit can now produce true, lasting magic items rather than only temporary or consumable effects. Each work takes a full day and materials worth the nearest listed item's value in gp (half from 20th level). Until 15th level you can use it only once a month

13th Level

Master Artisan

  • Effect: Once per encounter, one Kit ability costs no Ingenuity Points.

15th Level

  • Intelligence Bonus: permanent +1 Intelligence. It can take the score past 20, to 22 at most (see The Mortal Limit in Character Creation).
  • Lasting Work improves: once a week, as your Kit describes

20th Level

Renown: Workshop

  • Effect: You may found a workshop (see Renown in The Arneyan Codex); each season 1d4 apprentices (1st-level Artificers) join it. While you hold it, you may use Lasting Work once more each week (Construct Engineer upgrade limits are unchanged).

24th Level

Great Work

  • Effect: Gain the capstone creation unique to your chosen Kit, your Great Work: a singular, legendary work representing the height of your craft.

Kits: Disciplines of Craft

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Artificer folder. Drag one onto your character.

Every Artificer shares Tinker's Craft and Ingenuity Points.

  • Your Kit defines exactly what those resources build, from the 1st-level feature through to your Great Work at 24th.
  • The discipline is known as a craft of its own mainly in Tenor and Eltor.
  • The peoples, orders and places a kit names are examples, not the only ones: a kit suits anyone from a tradition like it.

Kit: Infuser

  • You don't build new things — you make old things briefly extraordinary.
  • A sword becomes flame for an hour.
  • A cloak becomes a wing.
  • Everything reverts eventually.
  • Infusers alone among Artificers are trained to work fine enchantment even through a full suit of plate — you are trained in all armour and shields.
  • You also choose one weapon at character creation to gain proficiency in, on top of your normal class weapon list — most Infusers pick whatever they intend to keep permanently enchanted.
  • Taught by the smiths of Dul Khagul, where the forge is the temple, and the enchanters of the Silver Tower.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Infuse Item: as an action, spend 1 Ingenuity Point to grant a mundane weapon, suit of armour, shield, or tool a temporary magical property from your known list (see Known options in The Artificer's Workshop) for 1 hour per level.
  • An infused weapon counts as magic while the infusion lasts.
  • Number of items infused at once equals half your level (rounded up).
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Sustained Working: your infusions last until you finish your next long rest instead of 1 hour per level, and being knocked unconscious doesn't end them early.
  • Kit Feature (5th): Layered Infusion: infuse a single item with two properties simultaneously for double the Ingenuity cost. Only one of the two properties may add damage.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Reflexive Infusion: for 1 extra Ingenuity Point, infuse an item as part of another action rather than using your whole action, and you may move one infusion to another item as part of your action.
  • Lasting Work (10th): Permanent Infusion: as often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and materials (see Lasting Work) to make one infusion permanent on a single item rather than temporary: for example, a blade that keeps Flametongue's fire damage forever, or a shield permanently etched with Ward-Etched's save bonus.
  • The item becomes a true magic item and no longer draws on your Ingenuity Points.
  • Name the item and give it a line of history: you are its maker.
  • AC and save bonuses from infusions do not add to an item's +N; use the higher.
  • Great Work (24th): The Everwork: choose one weapon, armour or shield: it carries every infusion property you know that fits it. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and materials as for Lasting Work. Unique: only one Everwork can exist per Artificer.

Kit: Construct Engineer

  • Your companion isn't summoned — it's built, bolted, and wound by hand, and it remembers every repair you've ever made to it. Taught in the workshops in the mountains between Tenor Hold and Eltor, where artificers began building automatons about a century ago.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Construct Companion: build a Small construct companion (d8 Hit Dice equal to your level; AC 14, +1 per four levels; attack bonus equal to a Fighter's BtH for a level equal to its Hit Dice, to a maximum of 24th; saves of half your level, minimum +1; immune to poison, disease and sleep).
  • Its attacks deal +1 damage per four Artificer levels.
  • It acts straight after your turn and follows spoken commands.
  • Commanding it is part of your turn and costs nothing; without a command it takes no action.
  • Spend 1 Ingenuity Point as part of your action: your construct regains 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier HP, or one of its hits this round deals +1d6 damage (+1d6 per four Artificer levels).
  • Example chassis: Guardian: Move 30ft, slam (1d8), +1 AC while adjacent to you; Scout: Move 40ft, climb 20ft, bite (1d6), Advantage on Perception; Striker: Move 30ft, blade arm (1d8).
  • You can have one construct.
  • If destroyed, it can be rebuilt over a long rest with parts worth 5 gp per Hit Die; it keeps its upgrades.
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Modular Chassis: the construct carries two utility mounts.
  • Kit Feature (5th): Reinforced Plating: the construct's AC increases by 2 and it gains Resistance 5 to one damage type of your choice, set at creation.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Independent Action: the construct carries two weapon mounts and attacks with either, and fights on without command if you fall.
  • Lasting Work (10th): True Construct: spend a full day and materials (see Lasting Work) to permanently upgrade your companion's chassis: each upgrade gives it 2 more Hit Dice and one permanent magical enhancement (flight, invisibility on command, a breath weapon dealing elemental damage, or similar), GM-approved. It can take one upgrade at 10th level and a second at 20th; replacing an enhancement later adds no Hit Dice.
  • Great Work (24th): The Masterwork Automaton: your companion undergoes a final transformation: +4 HD, it gains a second attack, and it can cast one Wizard spell of 3rd level or lower, chosen when the work is finished, whenever you spend 2 Ingenuity Points per spell level, at your Artificer level and Class Save DC. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and materials as for Lasting Work.

Kit: Gadgeteer

  • Pockets full of things that shouldn't work as well as they do.
  • You're never quite out of options, just out of Ingenuity Points.
  • Taught among Tenor Hold's artificers, who make the rifles and repeating crossbows, and at Izziki Needlecheek's Scrap & Tinkerworks in Mournas.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Quickbuild Gadget: as an action, spend 1 Ingenuity Point to produce a single-use gadget from your known list (smoke bomb, grapnel line, shock glove, flash powder, etc.) — effect equivalent to a 1st-level spell or utility effect. You can hold built gadgets equal to your Intelligence modifier + half your Artificer level; extras go inert.
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Reusable Chassis: one gadget of your choice (a Grapnel Line or Shock Glove are popular picks) becomes reusable rather than single-use: it stays built, and each use costs 1 Ingenuity Point.
  • Kit Feature (5th): Rapid Deployment: once per encounter, out of turn, when you are surprised or ambushed, you may quickbuild a gadget; it costs 1 extra Ingenuity Point.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Expanded Toolkit: you know two more gadgets than your known options allow, and you can hold one more built gadget at a time.
  • Lasting Work (10th): Signature Device: as often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and materials (see Lasting Work) to build one permanent, unique gadget with a lasting magical effect (not single-use) tailored to your specifications with the GM: a boot that deploys Rapid Ascent for free once per day, a ring that emits Smoke Bomb's cloud on command, or a glove with an always-on Shock Glove charge are all typical examples.
  • Great Work (24th): The Impossible Case: a portable kit containing a permanent version of every gadget you've ever built, foldable into a case the size of a book.
  • Each gadget in it works once per encounter at no cost.
  • Requires a month of uninterrupted work and materials as for Lasting Work.

Kit: Alchemist

  • Less about the one perfect tool, more about the shelf of forty imperfect ones. Something in the bag always does the job. Taught among the guild alchemists who sell potions on the open market, and the Ysoki Society's tonic-brewers under Nhool Sizzlefang.
  • Kit Feature (1st): Brew Formula: during a long rest, brew formulas from your known list.
  • Each costs 1 Ingenuity Point (2 for a damaging one) and keeps until used.
  • You can hold brewed formulas equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Artificer level; extras go inert.
  • Kit Feature (3rd): Efficient Brewing: formulas cost 1 less Ingenuity Point to brew (minimum 1).
  • Kit Feature (5th): Combat Alchemy: brew a single formula on the spot as an action at double the normal Ingenuity cost.
  • Kit Feature (7th): Volatile Mastery: your bombs and harmful formulas deal an additional die of damage.
  • Lasting Work (10th): Perfected Formula: as often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and materials (see Lasting Work) to perfect one formula into a permanent-effect item (a ring that continuously radiates Draught of Clarity's protection, a self-refilling flask of Elixir of Vigour, or a blade permanently coated with Caustic Flask's acid) rather than a consumable.
  • Great Work (24th): The Panacea: brew a legendary elixir capable of curing any one affliction, condition, or injury when drunk, including things no ordinary Restoration-tier magic touches. One dose a year. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and materials as for Lasting Work.

Crafting & Materials

  • Infusions, gadgets and formulas made with Ingenuity Points need only your toolkit, anywhere. Gold and materials apply to Lasting Work, rebuilding a construct and your Great Work.
  • Deliberately kept loose rather than a rigid shopping list — where you are determines how crafting actually works, and the GM adjudicates specifics on the fly. This is the guide, not a strict table.

Large Towns & Cities

  • A proper market means materials are simply available.
  • Pay a gold cost (the GM sets this based on the effect's power, roughly in line with an equivalent item's price in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue) and acquire what you need with no search required.
  • This is the default assumption for most crafting downtime spent in Mournas or any similarly-sized settlement.

Remote Villages & Small Settlements

  • Limited stock.
  • Common materials are usually available, sometimes at a markup; anything specific or unusual has to be special-ordered (taking real downtime to arrive) or sought out personally.
  • The GM may call for a Persuasion or relevant Skill check to track down an uncommon component through local contacts.

Wilderness & Frontier

  • No market at all. Materials have to be foraged, scavenged, or hunted directly — the GM determines what's plausible to find in the area and calls for an appropriate check (Survival, Herbalism, or a relevant skill) before the material is actually in hand.

Kit Variance

  • Alchemist: The most flexible Kit by far — herbs, venoms, fungi, and minerals can genuinely be foraged in the wild with a successful Survival or Herbalism-type check, making Alchemists far less dependent on a market than the other three Kits.
  • Infuser, Construct Engineer, Gadgeteer: Lean on manufactured components — refined metal, gears, glass, wire — that are difficult or impossible to improvise from raw wilderness materials. These three Kits are much more reliant on a proper town or city market, or a well-stocked workshop back home, to actually craft anything substantial.

Tools Required

  • Regardless of location or Kit, an Artificer cannot use Tinker's Craft or any Kit crafting feature without their tools in hand — the toolkit matching their Kit (see Starting Equipment & Gear) or an equivalent toolset. No tools, no crafting, no matter how good the market is.

The Artificer's Workshop

  • The full catalogue of ready-to-use options for each Kit, plus guidelines for designing something new with your GM.
  • Known options: you know a number of options from your Kit's list equal to 2 + half your Artificer level (rounded down).
  • Each time you gain a level you may swap one known option for another.
  • A custom design agreed with your GM takes one known option, and the guidelines below are the benchmark for it.

Infuser: Known Infusions

  • Flametongue — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 fire damage on a hit, and ignites flammables
  • Frostbrand — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 cold damage on a hit, and once a round the target's speed is halved for 1 round
  • Shockgrip — Weapon deals an additional 1d6 lightning damage on a hit
  • Guardian Plating — Armour grants +2 AC
  • Featherweight — The item's slot cost is halved (round up) for the duration; if worn armour, its Strength requirement is waived
  • Returning Throw — A thrown weapon flies back to your hand immediately after the attack resolves
  • Ward-Etched — A shield adds +1 to all saving throws in addition to its normal AC bonus
  • Glowing Ward — The item sheds light in a 30ft radius, and its wielder gains Advantage on saves vs fear
  • Silent Step — Armour or boots grant Advantage on checks to move silently
  • Bloodhound's Edge — A weapon grants Advantage on checks to track a creature it has damaged within the last 24 hours
  • Reach Extended — A melee weapon's reach increases by 5ft
  • Truth-Etched — A tool grants Advantage on checks to detect forgeries, lies, or magical disguises while in use
  • Deadweight — A weapon has Advantage on attacks against a target that is Restrained, Prone, or otherwise immobilised

Designing a Custom Infusion

  • Benchmark: A single Infusion should do roughly one of the following — add a damage die (1d6 of a chosen type), grant a flat +1 or +2 to one specific roll or AC, provide a narrow at-will utility effect (light, minor detection, a movement quirk), or impose a specific condition on a hit (halved speed, Disadvantage on the target's next save).
  • Avoid stacking two of these into one Infusion unless it's the result of Layered Infusion (5th level) or Lasting Work.
  • A custom infusion's damage is always 1d6; otherwise it may grant Advantage on one roll.

Construct Engineer: Known Chassis Mods

  • Blade Arm (weapon mount) — 1d8 slashing melee attack
  • Cannon Arm (weapon mount) — 1d6 force damage, 30ft range
  • Piercer Arm (weapon mount) — 1d6 piercing melee attack that ignores a shield's AC bonus
  • Grasping Claw (utility mount) — Advantage on grapple attempts; can retrieve small objects at your command
  • Lantern Core (utility mount) — Sheds light in a 30ft radius, shutterable on command
  • Climbing Legs (utility mount) — Climb speed equal to normal move speed
  • Alarm Core (utility mount) — The construct cannot be surprised while active and alerts you the instant it's triggered or attacked
  • Vocal Mimic (utility mount) — The construct can repeat up to one sentence of speech it has heard, in the speaker's own voice
  • Reinforced Chassis (passive) — +2 to the construct's Hit Dice for its HP only
  • Balanced Frame (passive) — The construct gains +1 to its AC
  • Recall Ward (passive) — You can call the construct to your side from anywhere within 1 mile with a spoken word
  • Storage Cavity (utility mount) — The construct has a hidden compartment holding up to 4 slots' worth of items
  • Mounts and passives: a construct carries one weapon mount and one utility mount (two utility mounts from 3rd level and two weapon mounts from 7th: see the kit), swapped during a rest.
  • Passives are installed during a rest and count as known options.
  • A construct holds one passive, plus one more at 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level.
  • Each passive can be installed only once, and removing and reinstalling Reinforced Chassis adds no further Hit Dice.

Designing a Custom Mount

  • Benchmark: A weapon mount should deal damage in line with a simple one-handed weapon (1d6-1d8), scaled by attack type rather than by size.
  • A utility mount should grant one clear non-combat capability (movement, detection, storage, communication) rather than a combat bonus — if it starts granting damage or AC, it's a weapon mount or passive instead.
  • A passive mod should be a small, permanent numeric bump (+1 to +2) to one stat, never a whole new capability.
  • A custom option scales with you: if it deals damage, 1d6 per four Artificer levels (minimum 1d6); otherwise it may grant Advantage on one roll.

Gadgeteer: Known Gadgets

  • Smoke Bomb — Creates a 15ft radius heavily obscured area for 1 minute
  • Shock Glove — One creature within reach makes a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC: on a failure it takes 1d6 lightning damage and is Stunned for 1 round; on a success, half damage. A creature that recovers is immune to your Shock Glove for the rest of the encounter
  • Grapnel Line — Instantly close a 30ft gap to a solid anchor point, or pull a Medium or smaller target 15ft towards you
  • Flash Powder — Thrown, 20ft: a 10ft radius burst; creatures make a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC or are Blinded for 1 round
  • Adhesive Charge — Thrown, 20ft: the target makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC or is Restrained until it uses an action to break free (Strength check against your Class Save DC)
  • Distraction Decoy — A small mechanical decoy moves and makes noise on your command for 1 minute
  • Rapid Ascent Boots — One use — gain a 20ft vertical or horizontal jump-assisted burst of movement
  • Noisemaker Dart — Thrown to a point within 30ft — creates a loud, distinct noise there, no damage
  • Caltrop Scatter — Covers a 10ft square with caltrops: a creature entering it makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC or takes 1d4 damage and has its speed halved for the round
  • Pocket Ram — One use — a spring-loaded ram deals 1d8 damage to a door, lock, or barricade
  • Glass-Cutter Ring — Silently cuts a hole in glass or thin material large enough to reach through
  • Signal Flare — Fired into the air — visible for 1 mile in clear conditions, in a colour of your choosing

Designing a Custom Gadget

  • Benchmark: A combat gadget should land somewhere around a 1st-level spell's worth of effect — a single damage instance (1d6-2d6), a single save-or-suffer condition lasting 1 round, or an area effect no larger than 15ft radius.
  • A utility gadget should solve one specific problem (noise, light, a locked door, a gap to cross) rather than several at once, and should almost always be single-use unless upgraded by Reusable Chassis.
  • A custom option that deals damage scales as Fire Bomb does (+1d6 per five Artificer levels); otherwise it may grant Advantage on one roll.
  • No infusion, gadget or formula restores hit points.

Alchemist: Known Formulas

  • Fire Bomb — Thrown — 2d6 fire damage, plus 1d6 per five Artificer levels, in a 10ft radius, Reflex save for half
  • Elixir of Vigour — Drink to gain temporary HP equal to 1d8 + Intelligence modifier
  • Caustic Flask — Thrown, 20ft: the target makes a Reflex save against your Class Save DC or takes 1d6 acid damage a round for 3 rounds
  • Draught of Clarity — Drink for Advantage on your next saving throw vs a mind-affecting effect within 1 hour
  • Smoke Powder Bomb — Thrown, 20ft: as the Gadgeteer's Smoke Bomb
  • Sovereign Glue — Bonds two objects together permanently, or until dissolved by a specific solvent
  • Universal Solvent — A few drops dissolve any adhesive on contact, including your own Sovereign Glue (the Catalogue's Slippery Oil does the same)
  • Draught of Steady Hands — Drink for Advantage on your next Dexterity-based check within 1 hour
  • Numbing Salve — Applied to a wound: the recipient ignores the effects of one level of Exhaustion for 1 hour
  • Choking Gas Vial — Thrown, 20ft: a 10ft radius; creatures make a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC or can't speak or cast verbal spells for 1 round
  • Quickfoam — Thrown at a fire or flammable area — extinguishes flames in a 10ft radius instantly
  • Reagent of Revealing — A few drops on a surface reveal invisible writing, residue, or a recently-handled object's last handler (GM discretion)

Designing a Custom Formula

  • Benchmark: A thrown or drunk formula should land at roughly a 1st-level spell's potency — 2d6 damage in a small area, a single round of a save-or-suffer condition, or a flat, narrow buff (Advantage on one specific roll type, or temporary HP equal to a small die plus Intelligence modifier).
  • Formulas that grant information or utility (detection, identification, minor restoration) should require a genuine cost — a rare ingredient, a full round to apply, or a limited number of uses — rather than being free and repeatable.
  • A custom option that deals damage scales as Fire Bomb does (+1d6 per five Artificer levels); otherwise it may grant Advantage on one roll.
  • No infusion, gadget or formula restores hit points.
